Messages.Author: echia...@yahoo.com
Messages.Body:


The difference is that normally when you have a Master card with the
clan requirement symbol, you must have a *ready* member of that clan in
order to play it.

The text of Feral Spirit however is:

"Put this card on any Gangrel or Gangrel antitribu you control."

The key difference (at least that I can see) is that you can put Feral
Spirit on a *non-ready* Gangrel/!Gangrel (such as one in torpor).

You can't have your cake and eat it too. Feral Spirit has the advantage
of being playable on torpored critters, but the flipside is that since
it doesn't technically require Gangrel (in the traditional sense since
you don't need a ready one), Tatiana cannot play it.

* Pedantry Addendum: Note that Carnivale also exists in an abnormal
state. It does not technically require Toreador ("Put this card on a
ready Toreador"). And while it does require the recipient to be ready
(unlike Feral Spirit) the difference here is that you don't actually
need to control the Toreador (give it to someone else's vampire).

According to the rulebook,

"Some cards will have other requirements (such as capacity or title)
stated in the card text. Only a minion who meets the requirements given
on a minion card can play it, while only a Methuselah who controls a
ready minion who meets the requirements of a master card can play it."

So both card text and the symbol on the bar can qualify as a
requirement. But since the specifications for a Master card refer to "a
Methusaleh who controls a ready minion who meets the requirements",
that would preclude Feral Spirit (not necessarily "ready") and
Carnivale (not necessarily "controls") from meeting that definition.

So based on this analysis I would argue that neither Feral Spirit or
Carnivale qualify as "requiring" their respective clans.

(Please note the difference between "require" in the vernacular sense
and "require" in the specific VTES terminology)
